33f57805e107666e: KUALA LUMPUR: The Yang di-Pertuan Besar of Negri Sembilan Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir has revoked the appointments of members of the state executive council with immediate effect, according to a statement issued by Istana Besar Seri Menanti on Sunday.
The palace said the decision was made after the exco members were found to have breached their oath of office.
It said the members had taken and signed their oath and pledge of allegiance before the Yang di-Pertuan Besar on Aug 7, before their appointment to the State Executive Council.
Under Article XXXVIII(5) of the Laws of the Constitution of Negri Sembilan 1959, an exco member, other than the Menteri Besar, holds office at the pleasure of the Yang di-Pertuan Besar.

The palace said the exco members had pledged allegiance to the Ruler and the Royal Institution, undertaken to protect and preserve the sovereignty of the state Constitution, and acknowledged the authority vested in the Dewan Keadilan dan Undang.
"However, they have breached that oath by their actions and statements on Sept 15," the statement said.
The Ruler subsequently revoked their appointments with immediate effect, with each affected member informed individually by letter.

Following the decision, Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim is required to submit a list of candidates for new members of the State Executive Council for the consideration and consent of the Yang di-Pertuan Besar, in accordance with Article XXXVIII(2) of the state Constitution.
The Ruler also expects the Menteri Besar to ensure that the administration of Negri Sembilan continues without disruption and in accordance with the state Constitution.
The palace stressed that the interests of the people must remain safeguarded during the transition.
The statement was issued by Datuk Azizi Mohamad Ali, Comptroller of the Royal Household of Istana Besar Seri Menanti, and dated Sept 20, 2026.

90cbc76d2fd21f13: MADRID: Atletico Madrid edged 10-man Real Madrid 2-1 in a La Liga derby clash on Sunday to leave Jose Mourinho's side trailing leaders Barcelona by six points.

Dean Huijsen was sent off early in the second half for Los Blancos before Alejandro Grimaldo and Jonathan David's goals earned Diego Simeone's Atletico victory, with Antonio Rudiger pulling one back late on.
Atletico rose to second, five points behind Barca and one ahead of Real Madrid, who chalked up a second defeat of the campaign.
The game hinged on Huijsen's red card early in the second period, for pulling down Giuliano Simeone in the box which led to a penalty, tucked away by Grimaldo to set Atletico on their way.
Mourinho started with Aurelien Tchouameni in midfield over Bernardo Silva, opting for defensive clout over creativity.
There was more tension than footballing quality in the first half, with neither side capable of creating any clear chances.
The main talking point was an incident between Jude Bellingham and Atletico defender Cristian Romero.

The England international threw himself into a tackle and Romero trod on his leg, with Bellingham booked initially, but after a VAR review the referee removed the card and issued it to the Atletico man.
Madrid were also unhappy with a heavy tackle by Lee Kang-in on Federico Valverde which went unpunished just before half-time.
It was a scrappy battle, intense but lacking excitement comparative to the star power on the pitch, especially in Madrid's front line, with Vinicius Junior, Kylian Mbappe and Bellingham kept quiet.
The game burst into life early in the second half when Huijsen pulled back Giuliano Simeone's arm as the forward ran through on goal and Atletico were awarded a penalty.
Huijsen was dismissed after a VAR review and Grimaldo beat Madrid goalkeeper Thibaut Courtois from the penalty spot.
Mourinho reacted immediately by replacing the underwhelming Vinicius and Arda Guler and sending on club record signing Yan Diomande and Rudiger.
It was Atletico who struck next, though, with Canada international David tucking away Giuliano Simeone's raking low cross on 59 minutes for his third goal in three matches.
The hosts came close to getting a third but Courtois made an excellent save to deny Julian Alvarez and Ibrahima Konate reacted brilliantly to head Grimaldo's effort from the rebound off the line.
Atletico goalkeeper Jan Oblak saved from Diomande and Bellingham rowed with Giuliano Simeone as Madrid's frustrations showed, impotent to change the course of the game.
Madrid pulled a goal back in the final stages with Rudiger heading Bernardo Silva's cross past Oblak. However, it was too little too late for Mourinho's side. -AFP
dddeabc5b1bf97ce: RAMALLAH: An Israeli settler was shot dead in the occupied West Bank on Sunday on the eve of the Yom Kippur holiday, and the military said it arrested the suspected gunman.
Israel's military also reported a car-ramming attack attempt in the West Bank, in which the perpetrator was killed.
Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu denounced the shooting as a "murderous attack" carried out ahead of the most important holiday for Jews, which will start on Sunday evening.

Beilinson Hospital, in the central Israeli city of Petah Tikvah, said that the Israeli man from the first attack, carried out near the Israeli settlement of Neveh Tzuf, north of Ramallah, had died of his wounds.
Israel Gantz, the head of the Yesha Council, the main representative organisation for West Bank settlers, said the deceased man was one of their number.

"IDF soldiers apprehended the suspect who carried out the shooting attack," the army said in a statement, adding that it located him at a hospital, which Palestinian sources said was in the city of Ramallah.
The army said a soldier had earlier shot and wounded the suspected assailant at the scene of the incident near Ramallah in the central West Bank.
Israel's army chief Lieutenant General Eyal Zamir said at the site of the attack that the military remained "on high alert, deployed and prepared with soldiers reinforced across all sectors."
AFP journalists reported that many checkpoints in that part of the West Bank had been closed or conducting searches in vehicles.
"We will impose a closure on the village and conduct investigations, through which we will reach everyone who assisted the suspect," Zamir said.
-'MAKE THEM PAY'-

"No one is immune, nor are those who aided them. We will settle the score with all of them: in Gaza, in Lebanon, and in Judea and Samaria," Netanyahu said, referring to the various fronts where Israel's military is active.
Israeli President Isaac Herzog said in a statement that he shared the victim's family's grief.
"On the eve of this sacred festival, let it be stated clearly: Terror will not break us, and it will not shake our spirit," he said.

Separately, the military said its troops had eliminated a man "who attempted to carry out a ramming attack against IDF soldiers operating in the Ganim area," a newly re-established settlement in the West Bank, near the Palestinian city of Jenin.
The Palestinian health ministry identified the attacker as Sami Zwaideh, 32, whom it said Israeli forces shot and killed in the Jenin area.

Israel has occupied the West Bank since 1967. More than 500,000 Israelis live in settlements in the Palestinian territory, which are illegal under international law, among some three million Palestinians.
According to an AFP tally based on data from the Palestinian health ministry, Israeli forces or settlers have killed more than 1,100 Palestinians in the territory since the start of the Gaza war.
Israeli figures show at least 49 Israelis, including civilians and security personnel, have been killed in Palestinian attacks or during Israeli military operations during the same period.--AFP

2dd63ddf2294af8a: GLASGOW: Rangers beat rivals Celtic for the second consecutive weekend as Ryan Naderi's strike earned a 1-0 away win that enlivens the Scottish Premiership title race.

Derek McInnes's men blew away their old rivals to win a League Cup tie 3-0 at Ibrox last weekend as he becomes the first manager since 1991 to win his first two Old Firm encounters.

Kim Min-su's strike from the edge of the box was parried by Viljami Sinisalo into the path of Naderi who tapped into an empty net.

Despite there being no away fans allowed to attend, Rangers dominated the second half and should have added to their lead.

Rangers, though, needed only the one goal as a Celtic side lacking inspiration rarely threatened to hit back and were met by a chorus of boos from the disgruntled 60,000 home fans at full-time.--AFP

2c701d91779421b9: ROME: Italy will ban burqas and niqabs in schools and limit the number of foreign students per class, far-right Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni said Sunday.
Italy is a frontline country for migration, and integration is a major campaign issue ahead of a general election next year.

"A measure will soon be presented to a cabinet meeting to legally establish a maximum number of foreign students per class," Meloni told a gathering of the youth wing of her Brothers of Italy (FdI) party.
"It also requires parents of foreign students facing serious difficulties integrating into the school system to learn Italian, and bans burqas and niqabs in schools," she said.
A crackdown on the use of burqas in schools was called for in July by the National Future (FN) party.
The FN, which is not part of the governing coalition, is further to the right than Meloni's and has emerged as a major challenger, rising sharply in the polls since launching in February.

While there is no law in Italy that expressly bans burqas, either in schools or in public places, a 1975 law prohibits the use of helmets or garments that make identification difficult without a justified reason.
In 2008, Italy's highest administrative court clarified that full-face veils may be worn for religious or cultural reasons provided that the face is revealed when identity verification is required.

The anti-immigrant League party, which is part of Meloni's coalition, submitted a bill to the Senate earlier this year that would ban helmets or garments except for in certain circumstances, such as sporting events or places of worship.
The limit on the number of foreign students per class already exists under Italian law, and Meloni did not spell out how that would change.
Foreign students account for just under 12 per cent of those enrolled in Italian schools, according to the National Statistics Institute (ISTAT).
Since 2010 the number of foreign students has been limited to 30 per cent of a class and of a school's enrolment.

The limit can be raised in cases involving foreign students with adequate language skills, such as foreign students born in Italy, or lowered when foreign students have a poor command of Italian.--AFP
1158d5496522518e: SAINT-PIERRE: French President Emmanuel Macron on Sunday welcomed Canada's Prime Minister Mark Carney to France's tiny North Atlantic territory of Saint Pierre and Miquelon, just off the Canadian coast.
The leaders' meeting was being held at a time when both their countries are experiencing strained relations with the United States.
They were expected to confirm Canada's close relations with both France and the European Union in a joint statement following a working lunch.
"In a world in crisis, our friendship is a strength," Macron posted on X, below a video of him welcoming Carney at the airport.
"Together, we affirm our sovereignty, our freedom to decide and our willingness to build a future of peace and prosperity," he added.
Macron's three-day visit to the French territory, a three-island archipelago of fewer than 6,000 people just 25km off Newfoundland, is the first by a French president in more than a decade.
The trip carries significant symbolic resonance.
The archipelago is France's only remaining possession in North America, a vestige of the vast territories Paris once controlled in what is now Canada and the United States.
Macron argues that US President Donald Trump's second mandate has reinforced his argument that Europe needs to become more sovereign, especially on security.

Carney, caught up in an intensifying dispute with US President Donald Trump – who has even threatened to annex Canada – has welcomed a proposal for his country to become the European Union's first "associate member."
Trump's repeated remarks about making Canada the 51st US state have been strongly rejected by Ottawa.--AFP

58d1d95d2cba434a: MELAKA: Malay Rulers cannot be treated as positions that can be changed according to political interests, as their status is governed by the Constitution and laws, says Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim.
He said those who had previously been vocal in defending the institution of the Malay Rulers should not question or reject the position of a Ruler when a decision did not suit their interests.
"In Negri Sembilan, those who have been making a lot of noise about the Malay Rulers, but when a decision does not go their way, they want to remove the Malay Ruler. I cannot accept that.
"We follow the Constitution and the law. If we can change the Ruler every month, the system of Rulers will fail.

"That is why the Federal Government is firm that the existing Yang di-Pertuan Besar of Negri Sembilan is legitimate and that any process to change the Ruler must follow what is stipulated in the Constitution and the law," he said when officiating the Chinese Cultural Night 2026 in Kota Laksamana here tonight.
He said the position of a Ruler must be respected based on the processes set out in the Constitution and laws, including those governing the legitimacy of a person holding the position.

He said the situation would become less stable if the institution of the Malay Rulers was turned into a political issue or if attempts were made to influence Rulers to make decisions according to the wishes of certain parties.
"It appears less stable because there are politicians who want to make it an issue. They want the Ruler to follow them.
"The Ruler must follow the Constitution. The Ruler must not follow politicians, or the state will be ruined," he said.

"If we are not angry today, after failing to win against a good team like Fiorentina, it certainly means we need to improve," Allegri told DAZN.

2df8acfda9548d6b: PARIS: Mathieu van der Poel warmed up for his bid for a second world title with a long-range solo break on the final stage of the Tour of Luxembourg on Sunday.

7cf2676d04babcf6: MINNEAPOLIS: Minneapolis Federal Reserve (Fed) president Neel Kashkari said on Sunday that inflation is too high across all sectors of the US economy, not just in rising oil prices.

"So even if we strip out energy, which is really volatile, and strip out food - they matter a lot - but in terms of where the economy is going, inflation is still too high," Kashkari told Fox News' "Sunday Morning Futures."
Kashkari supported the unanimous vote last week to raise interest rates by a quarter percentage point to 3.75%-4.oo%.
He was one of three officials to dissent at the Fed's prior meeting in favour of a hike when the majority of the Federal Open Market Committee then opted to leave rates unchanged.

Crude oil prices soared after hostilities intensified with the US and Iran attacking and sinking some oil tankers in the Strait of Hormuz and Saudi Arabia closing its vital East-West pipeline ​due to aerial attacks in the widening Middle East war.
"The Fed's job is to get inflation back down to our 2% target," he said, and there is nothing it can do with interest rates that will open up the Strait of Hormuz or bring oil prices down.

"The inflation that the American people are feeling every day is much beyond just oil prices. It's in all aspects of the economy. It's in the services sector, for example, widely. So we have tools to bring that back down," Kashkari said.
"Hopefully, we'll get some help from other parts of government or other parts of the real economy."
Kashkari's inflation concerns largely echoed those voiced by Fed chairman Kevin Warsh after the conclusion of the latest rate-setting meeting on Wednesday.
Warsh estimated that inflation as measured by the gauge the Fed uses to set its 2% target was likely around 3.6% in August, though that figure will not be released officially until later this month.

8a70c3cb92947742: SEREMBAN, Sept 21 — Negeri Sembilan’s Yang di-Pertuan Besar Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir has revoked the appointments of the state’s executive councillors with immediate effect, saying they breached their oath of office through their actions and statements on September 15.

In a statement last night, Istana Besar Seri Menanti said a member of the State Executive Council holds office at the pleasure of the Yang di-Pertuan Besar under Article XXXVIII(5) of the Laws of the Constitution of Negeri Sembilan 1959.

“His Royal Highness the Yang di-Pertuan Besar of Negeri Sembilan Darul Khusus has revoked the appointment of Members of the State Executive Council, Negeri Sembilan with immediate effect for violating their oath of office,” the statement said.
The palace said the exco members had taken and signed their oath and pledge of allegiance before Tuanku Muhriz on August 7, before their appointments to the council.

It said they had pledged allegiance to the Ruler and the royal institution, undertaken to protect and preserve the sovereignty of the Negeri Sembilan Constitution, and acknowledged the authority vested in the Dewan Keadilan dan Undang.
“They have breached that oath by their actions and statements on September 15,” the statement said.

The September 15 meeting was the one at which the state exco unanimously decided on an Instrument of Proclamation concerning Tuanku Muhriz’s removal and instructed the state secretary to proceed with its gazettement, according to Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim. Bernama reported that the state government had collectively decided that the proclamation removing Tuanku Muhriz was valid.
The palace said each affected exco member had been individually informed of the revocation in writing.
Ismail has been directed to submit a list of candidates for a new State Executive Council for Tuanku Muhriz’s consideration and consent, pursuant to Article XXXVIII(2) of the state constitution.

The Ruler also expects the menteri besar to ensure the administration of Negeri Sembilan continues without disruption in accordance with the state constitution and that the interests of the public are safeguarded, according to the statement.
The revocations come amid a constitutional dispute over Tuanku Muhriz’s position.

The Dewan Keadilan dan Undang said on September 17 that Tuanku Muhriz remained the lawful Yang di-Pertuan Besar and that there was no vacancy in the position. It also said the state exco and state government had no jurisdiction to determine the validity of the proclamation or the Ruler’s position.

The Attorney General’s Chambers later said the April 19 proclamation concerning Tuanku Muhriz’s removal was invalid because it did not comply with the mandatory requirements of Article 10 of the state constitution.

The AGC also said there was no evidence that any of the disqualification grounds under Article 10(1) applied to Tuanku Muhriz, and that the menteri besar and state exco had no unilateral power to remove him or declare the office vacant.

It said any attempt to gazette or implement the proclamation would be unconstitutional and invalid, and noted that the matter was before the High Court in Seremban, where an interlocutory injunction remained in force.
e1d88dfbc936bf0a: RAMALLAH: An Israeli settler was shot dead in the occupied West Bank on Sunday on the eve of the Yom Kippur holiday, and the military said it arrested the suspected gunman.
Israel's military also reported a car-ramming attack attempt in the West Bank, in which the perpetrator was killed.
Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu denounced the shooting as a "murderous attack" carried out ahead of the most important holiday for Jews, which will start on Sunday evening.

Beilinson Hospital, in the central Israeli city of Petah Tikvah, said that the Israeli man from the first attack, carried out near the Israeli settlement of Neveh Tzuf, north of Ramallah, had died of his wounds.
Israel Gantz, the head of the Yesha Council, the main representative organisation for West Bank settlers, said the deceased man was one of their number.

"IDF soldiers apprehended the terrorist who carried out the shooting attack," the army said in a statement, adding that it located him at a hospital, which Palestinian sources said was in the city of Ramallah.
The army said a soldier had earlier shot and wounded the suspected assailant at the scene of the incident near Ramallah in the central West Bank.
Israel's army chief Lieutenant General Eyal Zamir said at the site of the attack that the military remained "on high alert, deployed and prepared with soldiers reinforced across all sectors".
AFP journalists reported that many checkpoints in that part of the West Bank had been closed or conducting searches in vehicles.
"We will impose a closure on the village and conduct investigations, through which we will reach everyone who assisted the terrorist," Zamir said.

"No terrorist is immune, nor are those who aided them. We will settle the score with all of them: in Gaza, in Lebanon, and in Judea and Samaria," Netanyahu said, referring to the various fronts where Israel's military is active.
Israeli president Isaac Herzog said in a statement that he shared the victim's family's grief.
"On the eve of this sacred festival, let it be stated clearly: Terror will not break us, and it will not shake our spirit," he said.

Separately, the military said its troops had eliminated a man "who attempted to carry out a ramming attack against IDF soldiers operating in the Ganim area," a newly re-established settlement in the West Bank, near the Palestinian city of Jenin.
The Palestinian health ministry identified the attacker as Sami Zwaideh, 32, whom it said Israeli forces shot and killed in the Jenin area.

Israel has occupied the West Bank since 1967. More than 500,000 Israelis live in settlements in the Palestinian territory, which are illegal under international law, among some three million Palestinians.
According to an AFP tally based on data from the Palestinian health ministry, Israeli forces or settlers have killed more than 1,100 Palestinians in the territory since the start of the Gaza war.
Israeli figures show at least 49 Israelis, including civilians and security personnel, have been killed in Palestinian attacks or during Israeli military operations during the same period.

15eff95a503afc56: BOURNEMOUTH: Striker Alexander Isak scored the only goal of the game just before the hour mark to give Liverpool a 1-0 Premier League win away to AFC Bournemouth on Sunday, a victory that masked his side's struggles in attack.

The Swede has netted four times in the league as Liverpool remain unbeaten going into the international break but once again their front players struggled to gel, despite being able to call on the attacking talents of Cody Gakpo, Florian Wirtz and Bradley Barcola.

Isak's goal came about thanks to a Gakpo raid down the right but he was not the intended target; instead, the ball bobbled to him after Wirtz had been challenged by Bournemouth defender James Hill, and he slotted it home with a controlled finish in the 57th minute.
Other than that, there was little for Liverpool coach Andoni Iraola to celebrate on his return to Bournemouth after leaving them when his contract expired in June.

"It's very important for us to get goals, Alexander Isak included. It was a good win here, a clean sheet and we go to the international break before bracing ourselves for a very intense period," Liverpool captain Virgil van Dijk said.

Barcola looked lively on the left and Gakpo was a willing foil on the opposite flank but Wirtz - for whom Liverpool paid a reputed £100 million (US$134.64 million) last summer - put in another muted performance as the Reds managed a measly six efforts on goal in the game.

"Let's all stay calm and keep working and not get ahead of ourselves. This was an important win at a difficult ground. We could have done a lot better but we come away with the three points and a clean sheet," Van Dijk said.--REUTERS
72be294864a49ab4: MANCHESTER: Manchester City moved to the top of the Premier League in explosive style as Enzo Fernandez's first goal for the club lit the fuse on a pulsating 5-3 win against Sunderland on Sunday.
Argentina midfielder Fernandez, signed from Chelsea for a £125 million (US$167 million) on transfer deadline day, started the goal spree with his early strike at the Etihad Stadium.
Brian Brobbey led Sunderland's fightback, equalising after Fernandez's opener and cancelling out Rayan Cherki's goal.
Antoine Semenyo's brace kept City in front before Brobbey completed his hat-trick to put Sunderland back within one goal of Enzo Maresca's side.
Erling Haaland netted in the closing stages to seal City's seventh successive win in all competitions this season.
City have the only perfect record left in the Premier League this season and sit three points above champions Arsenal heading into the international break.
It has been a dream start for Maresca as he tackles the daunting task of replacing Pep Guardiola, who won 20 trophies in a golden era with City before resigning at the end of last season.

City have climbed to the top of the table with 13 goals in five league games, although, with games against Liverpool and Paris Saint-Germain immediately after the break, Maresca will be concerned about the defensive issues exposed by Sunderland.
Fernandez put City ahead after just nine minutes with a curling free-kick that caught Sunderland goalkeeper Robin Roefs off guard as it flashed past him at the near post.
Sunderland hit back impressively as Brobbey took Enzo Le Fee's pass and steered a clinical finish past Gianluigi Donnarumma in the 12th minute.
Cherki restored City's lead in the 29th minute, the French forward prodding in after Sunderland made a hash of clearing the danger.
City's defensive flaws were exposed by Brobbey again in the 33rd minute.

Le Fee and Thomas Meunier combined to tee up Brobbey as City failed to react quickly enough to stop the Dutch forward converting from close range, with the goal finally allowed after a three-minute VAR check for a potential offside.
A breathless half climaxed when Semenyo drilled past Roefs for his first goal of the season in the 43rd minute.
City defender Marc Guehi stumbled as he tried to reach Cherki's pass, but the ball ran towards Semenyo and the Ghanian forward lashed home from close range.
Semenyo was on target again in the 52nd minute, pouncing on Cherki's pass with a composed strike after more sloppy Sunderland defending.
Just as City looked set to run riot, Brobbey completed his treble two minutes later.
Nilson Angulo's pass was already rolling towards the net, but Brobbey ensured Guehi couldn't clear as he tapped in.
With no let-up in the frantic tempo, City defender Ruben Dias nearly gifted Sunderland an equaliser, inadvertantly guiding the ball towards his own net before hacking it to safety.
Haaland ensured City could relax at last in the 81st minute, finishing in typically predatory fashion at the far post for his seventh goal in six games this season.--AFP

43f515f85b6e16e7: PETALING JAYA: Perdana Menteri Anwar Ibrahim sekali lagi menegur parti politik untuk tidak menggunakan isu perkauman bagi menarik sokongan.
Taktik itu, katanya, sering digunakan jika parti politik berada dalam keadaan terdesak, terutama ketika berlaku dinamika politik yang tidak menguntungkan mereka.

“Kemudian politiknya simpang-siur, gaduh-gaduh. Bila dah gaduh, semua tarik sokongan, guna isu kaum. Bila terdesak, guna lagi isu kaum,” katanya pada Majlis Perasmian Pesta Kebudayaan Cina Malaysia kali ke-41 di Kota Syahbandar, Melaka, malam ini, lapor Bernama.
Turut hadir, Menteri Pembangunan Usahawan dan Koperasi Steven Sim dan Setiausaha Kerajaan Negeri Melaka Salhah Salleh.
Anwar berkata, Malaysia telah mencapai kemerdekaan sejak 69 tahun lepas dan isu perkauman seharusnya tidak lagi menjadi keutamaan mana-mana masyarakat yang tinggal di negara ini.
Masuk hampir 70 tahun kemerdekaan negara, katanya, Malaysia perlu tampil sebagai negara yang tumbuh dengan kekuatan pelbagai kaum tidak kira siapa yang memimpin negara.
“Ucapan malam ini lebih kepada rayuan. Rayuan supaya kita kembali dengan kekuatan. Setiap suara dikira. Untuk survival kita. Tak habis lagikah, bincang, gaduh. Negeri siapa? Negeri kita.
“(Di tahun) 40an, 50an, saya faham. (Negara) baru nak merdeka, masing-masing bicara soal 'survival' kaum mereka. 60an ya, (Malaysia merupakan) negeri baru,” katanya.
Beliau menambah, sekarang semua suara harus bercakap soal kelangsungan masa depan Malaysia sebagai satu negara yang bersatu.
"Siapa sahaja diberi mandat, siapa sahaja disokong, mesti janji menjaga rakyat, menjaga negara, menjaga masa depan anak-anak kita sebagai satu negara,” katanya.

394d4b480b355b99: MELAKA: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has called on all parties to stop using racial issues to gain political support, saying Malaysia should not remain trapped in such disputes nearly 70 years after independence.

He said such divisions were not new to Malaysian politics, with disagreements and attacks between political parties eventually leading to racial issues being exploited, particularly when certain parties were desperate for support.
"When I say 'our country', I do not mean that I want to undermine the position of others, no. We accept the rights of the Malay Rulers and what is enshrined in the Federal Constitution.

"But it is important to stress that our children should not feel like strangers in their own country. In the 1950s, I understand, we were newly independent and everyone was talking about the survival of their respective communities.
"In the 1960s, the country was still new. Fortunately, we had Tunku Abdul Rahman, Tun Razak, Tun Tan Siew Sin and Tun Sambanthan, who thought about what was best for the country.

"Then politics became complicated. We fought. When we fought, we attacked each other, withdrew support and used racial issues. When people became desperate, they used racial issues," he said when officiating the Chinese Cultural Night 2026 in Kota Laksamana here tonight.
Also present were Entrepreneur Development and Cooperatives Minister Steven Sim Chee Keong and Melaka State Secretary Datuk Salhah Salleh.

Anwar said Malaysia had been independent for a long time and should not continue to be trapped in such disputes to the extent that children from different communities felt like strangers in their own country.
"How can any country survive like this? How many years have we been independent? (Almost) 70 years. Are we still not done discussing and fighting? Whose country is it? Our country," he said.
He said Malaysia was now at an important stage socially, culturally and politically, and all parties must have the courage to reject approaches that could undermine national spirit and unity.
"I want to stress that this is not a political issue, but an issue concerning Malaysia's survival as a country. We want Malaysia to be a country that belongs to all of us," he said.
Anwar said that as prime minister, he had a mandate to safeguard the interests of all Malaysians regardless of race.
"I must look after the Malays, I must look after the Chinese, I must look after the Indians, the Ibans, the Kadazans. If I do not, I am not fit to be prime minister.
"The prime minister must look after everyone, with courage and confidence," he said.
He said everyone entrusted with a mandate or given the people's support must be committed to safeguarding the people, the country and the future of their children as one nation.
"Whoever is given the mandate, whoever receives the support, must promise to look after the people, the country and the future of our children," he said.

11d05e1ce8393cb4: MELAKA: Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim has once again cautioned political parties against exploiting racial issues to gain public support. He said such tactics are often deployed when political parties find themselves in desperate situations, particularly when political dynamics work against them.

“When politics becomes convoluted and contentious, parties withdraw support and resort to playing the racial card. When desperate, they use race again,” he said when opening the Malaysia Chinese cultural festival here tonight.

Anwar said racial issues should no longer be the primary focus of any community and as the nation approaches nearly 70 years of independence, Malaysia must emerge as a nation that thrives on the collective strength of its diverse communities, regardless of who leads the country.

1f67f5640b2df27d: FIVE baby orangutans abandoned in an Indian forest have exposed a "massive" exotic wildlife trade, with traffickers smuggling increasingly rare species into the country, say experts.

They warn of a growing multimillion-dollar trade in endangered animals, including apes smuggled through war-torn Myanmar to feed demand among wealthy Indians seeking exotic status symbols to flaunt on social media.
"There have been several instances of exotic wild animals being found or seized across the country," said Sumanth Bindumadhav of Humane World for Animals India. "The scale is massive."
Critically endangered orangutans are native only to Indonesia's Sumatra island and Borneo, which it shares with Malaysia and Brunei.
Yet the five tiny orangutans were found by rangers in Balasore, in India's eastern Odisha state. Aged around 1½ years old, they are being cared for at a zoo. Indonesia has requested their return.

Bindumadhav's group, in a June report, detailed what it called a "rising trade in exotic wildlife", demonstrated by a "steep increase in seizures" that reflected a "surge in illegal trade". The report estimated India's exotic pet market at US$42.6 million in 2024.
Orangutans and gibbons, small apes, were being "increasingly trafficked into India" from Southeast Asia's rainforests, it added.
A senior official at India's Wildlife Crime Control Bureau said "thousands of social media influencers" were promoting exotic species as pets online, fuelling demand among followers.
"It is a huge market," said the official, who requested anonymity because they were not authorised to speak to the media. "Rich people keep them in their homes."

Under a government voluntary disclosure scheme, more than 40,000 people had registered exotic animals by February 2021, government data shows. The figure is likely only a fraction of those in private hands, analysts say.

"This is a figure from only those who registered themselves, so the true volume of it is potentially much larger and remains unknown," said Bindumadhav. "The true scale of it is actually quite frightening."
Former India head of global anti-wildlife-trade group TRAFFIC Shekhar Kumar Niraj said the surge in trafficking was also linked to a "rising number" of animals held in private hands.

"Private zoos have violated laws at a very alarming scale across the country," said Niraj. "Primates are very popular in zoos because they are very intelligent, like to interact with humans, the kind of thing zoos want."
Indian federal authorities did not respond to requests for comment.
The World Wide Fund for Nature-India (WWF-India) documented 56 seizures involving about 4,000 exotic animals in 2022 alone.
In October last year, Mumbai Customs officers arrested a passenger carrying two endangered gibbons stuffed inside a checked bag.
Other seizures in Mumbai last year included lizards, tree-climbing possums and dozens of venomous vipers.
In 2024, forest officials recovered a trafficked orangutan from a flat in Maharashtra state.
But such seizures represent only a fraction of the trade, experts warn.
"The scale of it is much, much bigger than what we see actually based on the seizure data," said Jimmy Borah of the environmental advocacy group Aaranyak.

Experts have previously raised concerns over Vantara, a vast wildlife rescue and conservation centre in Gujarat founded by Anant Ambani, son of billionaire Mukesh Ambani, over its intake of endangered species.
Vantara has consistently denied any wrongdoing.

Last month, it said it was taking "bold steps to reset its operations", had withdrawn all applications to import live animals and named former head of the global wildlife watchdog CITES, John Scanlon, to chair its governing council.
Exactly how the orangutans were brought to Odisha — more than 2,000km by sea and 7,000km by land —is not clear. Police have launched a criminal investigation.
Experts say in addition to airports and formal cargo routes, the land border between Myanmar and India's northeast is a key trafficking route.
"The northeast is important for seizures of live exotic animals, linked to cross-border movement from Southeast Asia," said Dipankar Ghose of WWF-India.
Authorities have seized other exotic primates in the region in recent years, smuggled on jungle routes across the frontier.
"We are talking about miles and miles of a very porous border," said Borah of Aaranyak.

"We're very, very happy to get it done on the first match."

e59dbec9bfdeac6f: The prospect of a new global interest rate-tightening cycle is coming into view as some of the world's top central banks raise rates and signal more may be needed to tame inflation fuelled by the Iran war.
Key rates are already much higher than the rock-bottom levels from the last hiking cycle that began in 2022.
But central bankers are under market pressure to show that they are prepared to raise them further to tame inflation expectations and rein in long-term bond yields at multidecade highs.
The Bank of Japan (BoJ) became the latest big central bank to tighten on Friday, following rate increases by the Federal Reserve (Fed) two days before and the European Central Bank (ECB) last week.
The Bank of England (BoE) left rates unchanged last week, but flagged that inflation pressures could require further action.
"Our policy phase has changed," said BoJ governor Kazuo Ueda as the bank signalled it was ready to keep pushing up borrowing costs.

The moves, while formally independent of each other, reflect a shared concern among policymakers that higher oil and gas costs resulting from the Iran war raise the spectre of a new cost-of-living squeeze just a few years after the inflation surge that followed the Covid-19 pandemic.

The shift marks a stark contrast with the mood barely a month ago, notably after a short-lived pact between the United States and Iran that encouraged investors and policymakers to bet on easing hostilities and a retreat of energy prices.
The collapse of that agreement—and the recent Houthi advance along the Red Sea coast marking a new threat to global oil supplies—have changed the outlook significantly.
"The expectation now is that energy prices will stay elevated for longer," said ECB vice-president Boris Vujcic in an interview published on Friday.

"If inflation remains high through the autumn and affects household incomes and consumer behaviour, that will also have a dampening impact on gross domestic product," he added, saying that future calls would be made on a "meeting by meeting" basis.

Two sources said last week further tightening was now on the cards. While a hike at next month's meeting could be in play, a move in December — which would be the ECB's third hike this year —is more likely.
Defying the very public demands of US President Donald Trump for a cut in rates, new Fed chief Kevin Warsh joined his colleagues in a move to raise rates last Wednesday.

In his post-meeting press conference, he noted he would be "hard-pressed to describe broad financial conditions as restrictive", a formulation that counters the argument that monetary policy is hurting the economy.

The Fed's unanimous decision to raise rates, coupled with Warsh's comments on Wednesday, were seen as laying the groundwork for further tightening and helped reassure investors about the central bank's commitment to fighting inflation.
"The Fed has regained some credibility after raising rates," said Andrew Lake, chief investment officer at Mirabaud Asset Management.
Updated quarterly economic projections showed 16 of 18 policymakers anticipate at least one more quarter-percentage-point hike by the end of this year.
"Our inflation problem is not just about energy," said Kansas City Fed president Jeff Schmid on Friday.
Compared with the last round, the current global central bank tightening cycle is expected to be far more muted because inflation is not rising as sharply.
Fed projections released on Wednesday show even the most hawkish US central bankers expect a 4.25 to 4.50 per cent policy rate range by the end of next year and to drop after that.

Even as it held rates on Thursday, the BoE said it might have to go up if the Iran war continues in a commentary interpreted by observers as a clear shift in tone that positions it to follow the Fed and ECB higher.

"The longer this goes on, the more difficult this becomes," said governor Andrew Bailey, one of three members of the bank's Monetary Policy Committee who signalled they could back a rise, after he voted to hold at this meeting.
The writer is from Reuters

e870976313369d93: WASHINGTON: US president Donald Trump said on Sunday that the triumphal arch he plans to build near Arlington National Cemetery in Washington would double as a "military complex" housing drones and snipers, as well as storing large quantities of ammunition.

The plans have drawn criticism from preservationists and others who argue they could alter or diminish historic landmarks.

In a social media post, Trump said that at the "strong request" of the military he had agreed to turn the 76m arch "into a top grade Military Complex/Triumphal Arch, to house, store, and have the rapid ability to use large numbers of drones, plus Snipers, on both the roof and plaza areas, and additionally have and hold large quantities of sniper ammunition in storage".
The White House and the defence department did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

36120a92926a693f: Medical science has made such huge strides over the years but one area still largely eludes its advance: the need for healthy human organs to replace diseased ones.
Deputy director-general of health Datuk Dr Azman Yacob said more than 12,500 patients in the country (the vast majority being kidney patients) are on the waiting list for organ transplants.
The increasing cases of diabetes and the proliferation of dialysis centres underscore the urgent need to address the growing epidemic of kidney failure among Malaysians.
A holistic approach that balances diabetes prevention with kidney replacement strategies is essential to alleviate a burden that threatens to cripple both individuals and society.

The issue is not a lack of expertise to carry out transplants in the country but a severe shortage of organ donors. Dr Azman also revealed that there are 1.3 deceased organ donors per million population in Malaysia.
Countries such as the United Arab Emirates and Spain have higher organ acceptance rates of 20 to 30 per cent per million population, he added.
Something is seriously not right if the nation recorded a mere 102 deceased donor pledges so far this year — even if it marked an improvement from 89 during the same period last year.

Clearly, this shortfall is not due to a lack of public awareness campaigns. While public awareness can always be improved, underlying barriers that discourage Malaysians from donating must be identified and addressed.
There is a disconnect between the 450,000 registered organ donors and the actual number of organs harvested.

Awareness campaigns must target not only individual donors, but also secure the explicit buy-in of family members so that they will notify medical personnel immediately when the time comes. Granted, making good on donation pledges may not be exactly the highest priority when families are confronted with unexpected deaths.

We need a system that goes beyond simply registering organ donors —one that includes periodic follow-ups with donors and their families. Offering incentives, such as priority access to free health screenings for pledged donors, could significantly boost engagement.
More broadly, we should dismantle cultural or religious taboos surrounding organ donations. Clearly, the shortage of organs is a public issue that demands greater attention.
As a last resort, Malaysia could consider legislation similar to Singapore's, where organ donation is mandatory unless the individual explicitly chooses to opt out.
But all said, we must fully exhaust and enhance all voluntary measures to boost organ donation before resorting to mandatory legislation.

eade6009a4c9356a: KUALA LUMPUR: Drugs continue to enter prison despite strict security checks on new inmates, singer and composer Muhammad Yasin Sulaiman said.

"There are a lot of drugs in prison, even with all the SOPs. They strip us and make us do squats to check," he said on the Dark Room Sessions (Sembang Seram) podcast.
He said inmates suspected of carrying drugs in their bodies were made to pass stool at the prison.
Yasin said the drugs were often compressed, sealed in plastic and swallowed.
"They swallow it, then wait until they pass it," he said.
He said crystal methamphetamine, commonly known as "Ice", was the most popular drug among inmates.
"In prison, the most popular is Ice.

The New Straits Times has contacted the Prisons Department for comment and is awaiting a response.

The Petaling Jaya Sessions Court acquitted and discharged Yasin on 3 drug charges in November 2023, but ordered him to be placed at Hospital Bahagia Ulu Kinta in Perak at the pleasure of the Sultan of Selangor.
The High Court subsequently overturned the acquittal in August 2024 and sentenced Yasin to life imprisonment and 16 strokes of the cane over the 3 drug offences.
However, the Court of Appeal in April 2025 allowed Yasin's appeal, acquitting and discharging him while maintaining the order that he be placed at Hospital Bahagia Ulu Kinta.
Yasin was allowed to return home earlier this month after spending more than four years in prison and Hospital Bahagia.
c2d80762e0e9107d: SHAH ALAM: Laporan awal berhubung isu pengurusan dan kerugian Lembaga Kemajuan Tanah Persekutuan (Felda) dijangka diumumkan minggu depan, kata Perdana Menteri Anwar Ibrahim.

08132abf1202f477: SHAH ALAM: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has fired a broadside at those who proclaim to uphold the royal institution, only to attempt to overthrow a ruler after an election.
Without naming any party or individual, Anwar questioned whether those involved had sought a mandate from voters to remove a ruler, in an apparent reference to the royal dispute in Negri Sembilan.
"Before the election, they proclaimed that they would defend the royal institution. After the election, the ruler was overthrown," he said in his speech at the Perintis Reformis Reunion Hi-Tea here.
Anwar said the federal government's position was to defend the constitutional monarchy and the ruler in accordance with state constitutions and the law.
"It is not political parties that determine who the ruler is, but heritage, tradition, culture, the Constitution and the law."

Anwar said any challenge must follow the proper legal channels under state law, adding that he would not obstruct such a process but disagreed with action outside those channels.
"I want to stress once again that the government machinery will be fully used to defend the system of Malay rulers," he added.
The Negri Sembilan royal dispute was centred on a proclamation seeking to remove Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir as Yang di-Pertuan Besar.

e903b0c840718745: TEHRAN: Iran's top negotiator said Sunday that Tehran had conveyed to Washington through mediators its conditions for reopening the strategic Strait of Hormuz, which it has blockaded throughout the Middle East war.
The two foes are locked in a stalemate months into the conflict that began with US-Israeli strikes on Iran in late February.

Tehran has since maintained a stranglehold on the Strait of Hormuz, a vital shipping route for the world's oil and gas, while Washington is pushing a campaign to choke the Islamic republic's ports and economy.

"Our messages and the explanation of our conditions have been clearly conveyed to the other party through mediators," said Iranian parliament speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf, who has acted as chief negotiator in talks to end the war.

"As long as the conditions are not met... and the US commitments are not honoured, it will be impossible to return to the situation from before the negotiations and to an open strait," he added, according to state television.
Mohsen Rezaei, the head of Iran's supreme national security council said on Saturday that the Islamic republic had conveyed its conditions to the US via mediator Qatar.
"Our conditions are an end to the war on all fronts, the release of our frozen funds and an end to the naval blockade," he said in an interview with Al-Jazeera.
Iranian authorities have said that mediator Pakistan's interior minister Mohsin Naqvi will travel to Tehran on Sunday for talks.
Iran's Khatam al-Anbiya central military command, meanwhile, issued a threat against the US on Sunday, in a statement carried by state television.

"We warn that if the US makes a mistake in dealing with Islamic Iran, all of that country's bases and interests in the region will become the target of continuous, effective and painful attacks, without any limit or restraint," it said.
a9d23610fc3581e1: SHAH ALAM: Perdana Menteri Anwar Ibrahim menegaskan bahawa jentera kerajaan akan digunakan sepenuhnya untuk mempertahankan sistem Raja-Raja Melayu.

“Majlis Kerajaan Negeri bermesyuarat guling raja, hak siapa? Masa menang pilihan raya ada kamu sebut dalam manifesto, 'kalau kami menang kami akan gulingkan raja?' Tidak ada.

304c1c3868916a52: PUTRAJAYA, Sept 20 — The return of the haze across parts of Malaysia has once again brought forest and land fires in the region into focus.
But as smoke spreads and satellite images light up with hotspots, the question of where the fires are and what caused them is not as straightforward as it may appear.
Malaysia’s response this time includes an offer of firefighting assistance to Indonesia, which reflects the fact that the haze does not stop at national borders.

Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi on Thursday said Malaysia had offered a Bombardier CL-415MP aircraft, three helicopters and 52 officers and personnel from the National Disaster Management Agency, Malaysian Maritime Enforcement Agency (MMEA) and the Royal Malaysian Air Force.
The offer was conveyed to Indonesian vice-president Gibran Rakabuming Raka during his four-day working visit to Indonesia. It will be referred to President Prabowo Subianto for approval.
The CL-415MP, operated by MMEA, is capable of aerial firefighting. It was previously deployed to South Sumatra in 2015, when it dropped 546,000 litres of water during a five-day operation.
Ahmad Zahid, who is also the National Disaster Management Committee chairman, said the offer to assist was to help Indonesia tackle transboundary haze, rather than interfering in its affairs.
The urgency is clear from the air quality readings in Malaysia.
As at 5pm on Friday, 32 areas recorded unhealthy Air Pollutant Index (API) readings.

According to the Malaysian Air Pollutant Index Management System portal, Johan Setia in Selangor recorded the highest reading at 183, followed by Shah Alam (169), Petaling Jaya (162), Banting (161) and Klang (159).

Sarawak recorded the highest number of affected areas, with Kuching recording an API reading of 174, followed by Samarahan (167), IPD Serian (166), Sibu (162), Bintulu (161), Sarikei (155), Sri Aman (154) and Kapit (153).
Putrajaya recorded an unhealthy reading of 172, while Batu Muda and Cheras recorded 167 and 165, respectively. Temerloh and Jerantut in Pahang recorded 155 and 151.
An API reading of 0 to 50 indicates good air quality; 51 to 100, moderate; 101 to 200, unhealthy; 201 to 300, very unhealthy; and 301 and above, hazardous.
For the public, the immediate concern is the smoke. For those trying to trace the fires, however, the picture is more complicated.
Indonesia was reported as saying that it was complying with Asean’s existing haze response mechanisms, including daily reporting of hotspot data, projected smoke movements and firefighting measures.
Asean activated a Level 3 alert for severe transboundary haze on August 26. Under the mechanism, member states share information to help neighbouring countries take precautionary measures.
At the same time, the haze has once again revived questions about the role of the palm oil industry in regional fires.

The Malaysian Palm Oil Board (MPOB), however, said regional forest and peat fires could not be attributed primarily to oil-palm cultivation, with satellite mapping currently showing hotspots across multiple land uses.
These, it said, include unmanaged areas, pulpwood plantations and small-scale farming plots.
Director-General (DG) Datuk Badrul Hisham Mohd said human land-clearing activities remained a major driver of fires, while severe climate anomalies such as El Niño could amplify their spread.
“From a scientific standpoint, El Niño and prolonged dry weather act strictly as environmental amplifiers, not the spark itself,” he told Bernama.
That distinction matters when looking at the fires.
Badrul Hisham said wildfires did not occur spontaneously in the region’s humid climate, with ignition generally associated with human activity.
Prolonged dry weather, however, reduces soil and vegetation moisture, allowing fires to spread more rapidly.
The problem becomes harder to manage in peat areas, where drained peat can dry out and burn below the surface.
Badrul Hisham said this can make fires difficult to detect and extinguish.
“Once ignited, peat fires can continue smouldering underground and may reignite even after surface fires appear to have been brought under control.
“The resulting emissions can continue for weeks or months and, depending on wind direction, contribute to prolonged transboundary haze,” he said.
When fire risk rises

The newly-appointed DG also stressed that the Malaysian oil palm industry should not be described as having a seasonal open-burning practice because zero burning has already been established within the industry through the mandatory Malaysian Sustainable Palm Oil (MSPO) Certification Scheme, enforced since January 2020.
It is the risk of fire that changes with the seasons, he said.

That risk generally increases during prolonged dry periods, particularly from June to September during the southwest monsoon, while some regions also experience a dry window around January and February.

Lower rainfall, declining soil and peat moisture and higher temperatures during these periods make accidental or unauthorised ignition more likely to spread, with El Niño capable of further intensifying the risk.
There is also a need to be careful when reading satellite hotspot maps.
A hotspot is an indicator of possible fire. It is not, by itself, proof of open burning or evidence of someone starting a fire.
“That distinction matters, because a hotspot can identify where a fire may be occurring, but not necessarily who started it, or what land use is involved.
“For Malaysia and Indonesia, therefore, the immediate challenge is twofold: containing the fires and improving the ability to identify their causes,” he said.
For now, Malaysia’s offer of aircraft, helicopters and personnel is focused on putting out fires.
But the wider haze problem is unlikely to be solved by firefighting alone.
Prevention, land management and early detection remain part of the equation, as does cooperation between countries sharing the same airspace and, at times, the same smoke.
The palm oil debate will continue, particularly whenever the haze returns.
Therefore, satellite hotspots alone cannot settle that debate. Fires occur across different types of land, and weather conditions can determine how quickly they spread and how long they persist.
That makes identifying the actual source and cause of each fire just as important as putting it out.
For Malaysia, Indonesia and the wider region, that may be the more difficult part of dealing with the haze. — Bernama
4a6b04ffefce7040: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 20 — Jazeman Firhan Jaafar, 33, has spent more than two decades in motorsport, from racing internationally and coming within reach of a Formula One seat to competing at Le Mans.
Today, the former Mercedes-AMG Petronas Formula One development driver is using that experience to open doors for Malaysian talent in motorsport and the wider automotive industry.

Through Persona Energy Sdn Bhd, the company he established in 2018, Jazeman runs the Technology Transfer Apprenticeship Programme (TTAP), giving Malaysian engineers, mechanics and other technical talents hands-on exposure to international motorsport and industry partners. “So, I have talents like that … they have the grit, the skill, but they don’t have that ‘door opening’. So, I open the door for them,” Jazeman told Bernama in an interview recently.

So far, 95 talents have gone through TTAP, with most already working in the industry while some have pursued further studies. Supported by partners including Porsche, Bosch Engineering and Yayasan Raja Muda Selangor, the programme exposes participants to areas ranging from race cars and data to vehicle components and engineering.

TTAP runs for seven months, with participants required to gain hands-on experience at three races during the programme. The locations vary according to the racing calendar, with participants potentially assigned to events in Malaysia, Japan, Thailand or Indonesia.

Jazeman said some are subsequently taken to additional races once the teams are comfortable with their performance. “So, my requirement is three races. I do a pre-event briefing. Then, we do a scorecard to see their performance and then their graduation,” he elaborated.
He wants TTAP to eventually become self-sustaining, with between 10 and 20 Malaysian talents integrated into the racing industry each year, before expanding the programme to talents across Asean.
From six-year-old go-karter to Europe

Jazeman’s own journey began almost by chance. He was six in 1998 when a friend of his late father invited him to try go-karting in Shah Alam. What began with rented or leased karts progressed to national and Asian championships. By eight, Jazeman had decided he wanted to become a Formula One (F1) driver. His mother, however, insisted that racing could not come at the expense of his education. “I had to promise her to never forget to ‘mengaji’ (study) first. You know, do my tuition first. And then I can go racing,” he recalled.

At 14, Jazeman was below the minimum age requirement for the Petronas Talent Development Programme’s Formula BMW programme. He instead secured an exemption from the FIA to compete in Formula BMW Asia and found his own sponsorship. He won the championship, beating the Petronas team. A day later, Petronas called and invited him to join its programme.

At 15, Jazeman moved to Europe, where he spent much of the next nine years pursuing a professional racing career. “I didn’t have a life like other teenagers did. I had to move, and I didn’t have many friends in Europe either. I probably had one friend who happened to study there. But then I built my contacts; I built my relationships with certain people from racing, and that led me to my professional career then. So, I was in the UK nine years in total. No easy feat lah,” he recalled.
Europe exposed him to a mature motorsport industry and eventually took him to the final step before F1.
The F1 deal that did not happen

After winning the Formula Renault 3.5 Series race in Monaco in 2015, Jazeman said he received offers from two F1 teams, Force India and Manor. Force India presented what he described as the stronger proposition: a one-plus-one-year deal, beginning as a reserve driver before progressing to a race seat. The challenge was securing the necessary financial backing within a limited timeframe.

Jazeman said a proposed funding structure involved Petronas, tourism and sports authorities as well as corporate sponsors. But the plan came amid political pressure surrounding the 1Malaysia Development Bhd controversy, while falling oil prices put pressure on Petronas.

He tried to salvage the offer, but the required commitments could not be confirmed in time. “They came back with a second offer to proceed with reserve driver (first). I still have the contracts in my mum’s house. But we couldn’t sign it because none of the sponsors could confirm at that time,” he recalled.

He subsequently redirected his career towards Mercedes-AMG and endurance racing, which offered the prospect of a longer professional career. “I’m honoured and blessed that I was given an opportunity. You know, I was on that final step. But I think we tried our best,” he added.

Jazeman acknowledged that they could perhaps have negotiated better, but said F1 deals required people who understood how to put the different elements together. Today, that chapter is closed. “So if you ask me again if I would try again, no. I think I’ve moved on from it,” he said.
Unfinished business

Jazeman has not, however, moved on entirely from racing. He has gone on to compete in GT and endurance racing and still believes he can perform at a high level. One race in particular remains unfinished business: the 24 Hours of Le Mans, the world’s premier sports car endurance race, won by the team covering the furthest distance in 24 hours.

Jazeman competed at Le Mans in 2018 in an all-Malaysian line-up with Weiron Tan and Nabil Jeffri, finishing fourth in the LMP2 class. “I have been honoured to have won big races. The list goes on,” he recollected. “If you put me in a race car tomorrow, I will perform at my utmost best. But Formula 1, no.”
Jazeman’s experience has also shaped how he views Malaysia’s search for another F1 driver.
He believes Malaysia has talent with the potential to build professional racing careers, although the pathway to F1 has become considerably more demanding as the sport has evolved.

Malaysia has talent capable of professional careers in GT, Le Mans and endurance racing, Jazeman reckons, but reaching F3, F2 and ultimately F1 requires more than funding, as it also demands enormous early sacrifices, including leaving home and building a career overseas as he did at 15.
The talent Malaysia left on the table
Having spent years racing overseas, Jazeman believes Malaysia has historically paid too little attention to developing the people behind the race car.

The country once had extensive links with F1 through Malaysian companies and organisations, yet much of that involvement remained commercial rather than being systematically used to develop local technical talent.

“Because a lot of the involvement in F1 was purely a commercial element. Not to grasp at talent development. Which is such a pity,” he said, adding that at its peak, Malaysian interests were connected with as many as four F1 teams. We had four F1 teams from a small country. But no F1 driver, no F1 engineer. So, I don’t know what the sole purpose of this commercial element was. Talent development or talent in the team should be the core. That is how I see it,” said Jazeman.

He is also convinced Malaysia has technical talent capable of working at the highest levels of motorsport. “You know, race teams, international race teams love hiring Malaysians because we speak English. I’m certain our talents can do it,” he added.
Beyond hosting
The question of what Malaysia gains from international motorsport is again relevant as Sepang prepares to host the Formula 1 Gulf Air Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia next month.

Jazeman noted that Malaysia already has the facilities and hospitality needed to host major motorsport events. Where Malaysia falls short, he believes, is in extracting more lasting benefits from the international teams and organisations that come here. “We have the opportunity to ask them for what we want. I feel that we do not capitalise enough on the spillover effects,” he added.

While Malaysia already benefits from business spillovers such as hotels and transport, Jazeman said more could be done in talent development and technology transfer. He pointed to the Fédération Internationale de l’Automobile (FIA) choosing Malaysia to host the International Karting World Cup twice as evidence that the country’s facilities and grassroots ecosystem have international recognition.

“Now, what falls short is that maybe we are a bit shy to squeeze from them what we want because we may not be paying for F1 today, but we still have the top teams coming here. We have the opportunity to ask (for) what we want. I feel that we do not capitalise enough on the spillover effects,” he reiterated.

Jazeman reckons Malaysia has at times placed greater emphasis on hosting major races than building the ecosystem beneath them. He said there was coordination among the Sepang International Circuit, the Motorsports Association of Malaysia and the Youth and Sports Ministry, but the government ultimately had to lead on what Malaysia wanted to develop.

“We had F1 that came here for many years, but we didn’t capitalise. So now, we have an interest to come back, and people want it to be back permanently, but we have to really plan for that integration … but it has to come from the ministry. You want to champion the best engineers of F1 of tomorrow; it has to come from them. You want the next F1 driver; it has to come from them,” he said.
For Jazeman, TTAP is one attempt to change that. He wants the programme to become sustainable, build more links with international teams and eventually extend its pathway beyond Malaysia.

After spending his youth trying to find a way into the highest levels of motorsport, he is now opening that door for others. “The door is open; you go for it. That is the only thing I can do, which I have done,” said Jazeman. — Bernama
d17c941c3f34adf1: CAPAS (Philippines), Sept 20 — Tribal leader Petronila Munoz walked across the sweeping Philippine grasslands she has called home for generations, uncertain about its future, as a sprawling tech hub for a US-led initiative takes shape.

With little information and no prior consultation, the Indigenous chieftain said her Aeta Hungey tribe was uncertain how much of their land could be affected or what will become of the livelihood it provides.
“There’s still no clarity,” Munoz told AFP inside the tribe’s traditional meeting hall.
“What will happen to us? That’s our biggest question.”

In April, the United States announced that the Philippines had joined Pax Silica, a US-led effort to strengthen supply chains for semiconductors and rare earth elements and reduce participating countries’ dependence on China.

The Philippines has designated a 1,620-hectare (4,000-acre) site in New Clark City in Tarlac province, north of Manila, for a manufacturing hub aimed at producing high-end components for use in artificial intelligence data centres.
The government estimates the initiative could attract up to US$70 billion in investment and create about 190,000 jobs, a major boost to a country with more than three million unemployed people.
The project has a long timeline. No tenants have been confirmed.
Plans to domestically process the country’s mineral resources could be even further away.
For about 1,000 Aetas, however, the prospect of displacement is already here.
In July, they received a letter from the Bases Conversion and Development Authority (BCDA) warning that the project “could affect your occupied lands”.
‘Money runs out’

Munoz said visiting BCDA employees told them to leave by December and relocate to an area about 16 kilometres (10 miles) from their current home, without providing a master plan showing which parts of their ancestral domains would be affected.
Munoz said the BCDA has offered them just 30 pesos (US$0.48) per square metre for their lands, an offer all declined.
“Our lives, our livelihood and our culture are tied to this ancestral land,” Munoz said.
“Land is more important. Money runs out.”
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->
Residents looking at a map with proposed projects by the Bases Conversion and Development Authority (BCDA) in Capas. — AFP pic
The BCDA declined to address specific questions about the Aetas’ situation and rejected a freedom of information request for the site’s official boundary map and geospatial data.
It said the information was being “withheld temporarily until the official action is finalized or published”.
At a Senate hearing last month, BCDA president Joshua Bingcang said the Aetas were living on government land. Like many Indigenous groups in the Philippines, they hold no land title.
Civic groups have also raised concerns about the project’s environmental impact, particularly the demand for water and electricity in a country plagued by droughts and rotational power outages.
The US Statement Department told AFP that “environmental, water, energy, and community-impact studies” would inform the project’s design.
“Before any major development happens, we expect rigorous stakeholder impact assessments will take place,” a spokesperson said.
Bingcang told the Senate that investors would be required to build their own power and water systems.
‘We have to open up’

Alvin Camba, research director at an AI firm focused on supply chains and risk assessment, said Manila’s close relationship with the United States could motivate investors to set up shop despite the power concerns.
Last month, reports said Washington planned to warn countries they could be excluded from Pax Silica if they joined a rival framework backed by Beijing.

“This is where the advantage of the Philippines comes in. The Philippines is the least affected by Chinese capital in South-east Asia,” Camba told AFP, saying the country would offer foreign companies the ability to “disentangle” from China.
For political economist Calixto Chikiamco, Pax Silica represents a “historic opportunity” for the Philippines to move beyond its traditional wheelhouse of microchip testing and packaging.
“We have to open up to foreign investment so that technology transfer (to the Philippines) will happen,” he told AFP.
Sacrifices
The BCDA has been conducting public consultations in Tarlac and nearby provinces, but the agency has yet to hold talks with her tribe, Munoz said.
The Aetas remain uncertain if the government would help them build new homes or provide land to cultivate for income if they are moved.
“I wish they would listen to us. They’re just talking among themselves,” she said, adding she worried her tribe would not be qualified for the sort of new jobs Pax Silica promised.
While a proponent of the initiative, Chikiamco said the government was doing “a terrible job” explaining the benefits and tradeoffs it represented.
Camba agreed: “I would actually advise the Philippine government to be very transparent about what’s happening. A big problem is transparency.”
Still, the benefits outweigh the risks, he said.
“Every country that has... jump-started development has had to make sacrifices,” Camba said.
But 63-year-old Munoz, who hopes to be buried in her tribe’s traditional burial ground, said she would not leave, even if a backhoe flattened her home.
“Why do we have to be the ones to sacrifice for the kind of development they want?” she asked. — AFP
1f13892aed776676: PETALING JAYA: DAP's decision that only secretary-general Loke Siew Fook should resign from the Cabinet over the conditional pardon granted to Najib Razak is inconsistent with the views previously expressed by its leaders, says prominent lawyer Haniff Khatri Abdulla.

Speaking in a podcast by Fazli Mohammad, he said all DAP members of the Cabinet should resign if the party was truly sincere about its stance on the matter. Their resignation would not amount to a withdrawal of support for Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim, as DAP's MPs could still back him in Parliament.
Yesterday, Loke said he would resign as transport minister, but DAP would remain in the government and its other ministers would stay in the Cabinet.
Haniff also singled out housing and local government minister Nga Kor Ming, saying he should have been among the first to resign given his earlier public remarks on Najib’s pardon.
“He repeatedly argued with (Umno Youth chief) Dr Akmal Saleh over the matter. If he is a gentleman, he should resign before Loke does,” he said.
Nga had vowed to resign if Najib was released from prison, in response to Akmal’s urging him to “fulfill his promise” to step down.
Haniff said political leaders should stand by what they promise publicly.

However, Oriental Daily quoted an unnamed DAP leader as saying that Nga had offered to resign during DAP’s central executive committee meeting yesterday, but was persuaded by Loke to remain in the Cabinet.
FMT has reached out to Loke and Nga for comment.

64ae84f5a2104bde: SHAH ALAM: Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim has denied allegations that he paved the way for the conditional pardon granted to former prime minister Najib Razak, saying that every prisoner has the right to apply for a royal pardon.

Anwar said the pardons board had the jurisdiction to evaluate applications by taking into account the advice of the prime minister and the attorney-general at the federal government level, while the final decision rests with the Yang di-Pertuan Agong.

“I wish to reiterate that every prisoner has the right to submit an appeal, and I defend that right for anyone, including Datuk Seri Najib. He has the right to submit his appeal for consideration by the pardons board and the king," Anwar said at a reunion gathering of Perintis Reformis this afternoon.

“There are discordant voices from our former allies claiming this is Pakatan Harapan's doing. As prime minister, I do not want to use harsh words; people can criticise me, but it is untrue. Those in government know my stance from the beginning. Even if you want to win votes, it should not be by lying. Claiming that I paved the way is incorrect,” he said.

Anwar said jurisdiction over pardons and the conferment of royal awards was under the discretion of the sultan and heads of states, or the Yang di-Pertuan Agong, in line with constitutional principles.

He said his previously expressed views on a pardon for Najib were not intended to influence the decision, but rather took into account current court cases, the substantial fine imposed on Najib, and its impact on public confidence in the justice system as well as international perception.
At the same time, Anwar stressed that granting a pardon does not impede legal proceedings against other ongoing cases, including those related to 1MDB and civil suits.
He said the government remained firm in combating corruption and ensuring that cases involving abuse of power are investigated and processed through the legal system.

Najib has been granted a conditional pardon, allowing him to serve the remainder of a six-year jail sentence under house arrest until Aug 23, 2028, subject to payment of a RM50 million fine and other conditions.
b6182c2f95976ea1: SHAH ALAM: Perdana Menteri Anwar Ibrahim menafikan dakwaan beliau membuka jalan bagi pengampunan Najib Razak, sebaliknya menegaskan bahawa setiap banduan berhak mengemukakan permohonan pengampunan untuk dipertimbangkan Lembaga Pengampunan.
